payload.claim: The holder's `fcntl.flock` grant (line 106) and its write of pid/text (lines 110-113) are not atomic. A contender that hits `BlockingIOError` in that narrow window reads whatever the file held before (empty on first use, or a stale line from an earlier, now-dead holder, since release never clears the file), so `LockHeld`'s reason can name a pid that holds nothing. This matches the spec's literal instruction ("the holder writes its own pid and that text into the file after it takes the lock"), so it is not a criterion violation, and no witness here can exercise it: every holder in the tests is already blocked on stdin or past its write by the time a contender attempts the lock.
